claims.claim: Thymus screening establishes nonmatching on the supplied finite panel and produces Candidate status; it does not externally admit a rule.
limitations: Empty panels pass vacuously.
No population false-positive bound or completeness proof.
Panel hash boundary collision is separately reproduced.

claims.claim: For positive K, n in1..16 and 0<t<1, the Hill threshold is equivalently S^n(1-t)>=t*K^n. With positive per-sensor cap c, activation requires at least the least integer q with (q*c)^n(1-t)>=t*K^n named positive sensors.
limitations: An inspection argument, not a mechanized proof of Rust.
Named sources need not be independent.
BigInt input magnitude is not bounded here.

claims.claim: Native support is an exact branch-and-bound maximum independent set over at most32 deduplicated supplied correlation-key rows; support>=3 yields provisional eligibility only.
dependencies: truth and adequacy of correlation metadata
limitations: Graph independence is not statistical independence.
Distinct observation digests in external-review assessment need not represent independent observers.
Compatibility replay/human_admit helpers do not perform full authenticated replay.

claims.claim: Signed custody verification binds ordered statement bytes, issuer/key/purpose/scope, declared rule/source/subject/context, evidence bytes, clock windows and legal chained state transitions.
dependencies: trusted policy and clock supplied by caller
durable latest tip held outside this function
limitations: Authenticates key-relative statements, not truth or human identity.
Caller can provide a valid historical prefix unless external tip pinning rejects it.
Reversed timestamp interval causes a pre-signature debug panic; no signature bypass shown.

claims.claim: Regulation computes a strict false-discovery threshold FP/(TP+FP) using exact widened arithmetic and checks telemetry target/current status.
limitations: Not FP/(FP+TN), not a population guarantee, and intentionally distinct from Python Signal1 toxicity.

claims.claim: Two-signal screening checks distinct observer/predicate/digest/span projections before disposition; the activation use case binds content bytes through injected ports.
limitations: Structural separation is not statistical independence.
evaluate_signals alone trusts projected evidence; evaluate_independent adds structural checks.
No detector completeness inference.

claims.claim: Native immunity implements shortest-hop BFS backward propagation and fixed-point forward taint, unlike the reviewed Python current-prompt/single-pass adapters.
limitations: No hard maximum10 is enforced by compute_backward_propagation.
This is graph reachability, not causality or effective protection.
Fixture confirms only the supplied three-node case.

claims.claim: Lineage witness digests bind named endpoints and relationship, and insertion rejects cycles; the digest is publicly computable from those declarations.
dependencies: caller provenance and graph mutation discipline
limitations: No observation, signed issuer or semantic causal proof is required.
Public maps permit bypassing insertion checks.
Generation cache is stale after some legal insertion orders.

claims.claim: For a well-formed stochastic graph, sparse F(r)=alpha*P*r+(1-alpha)u is an l1 contraction with alpha=17/20. The posterior bound alpha/(1-alpha)*||r_k-r_(k-1)||1=17/3*delta follows from geometric summation. The implementation computes rational steps and that exact scalar bound.
limitations: Inspection argument, not mechanized implementation proof.
Singleton branch skips graph validation.
is_converged tests delta<=tolerance, not certified_l1_error<=tolerance.
Compaction trusts its supplied certificate's error field.

claims.claim: Dense rank verification reconstructs transition entries, rejects a nonstochastic candidate vector or mismatched matrix, and checks the exact stationary equation.
limitations: Duplicate parent edges break row stochasticity in both implementations.
Rank port does not enforce all stochastic-domain assumptions.
A metric-relative rank is not semantic fitness, generalization, convergence of learning or task success.

claims.claim: Foundation and Python-compatible planar substitution replace one typed input with ordered inner inputs. Structural associativity checks compare signatures for specified triples.
limitations: Does not compare operation behavior or establish equality of full Operation records.
Signature tests do not prove associativity of arbitrary actions or effects.

claims.claim: The kernel normalizer validates reconstructed operation/port data, including Admitted trees, substitutes matching open leaves, erases identity/association syntax and hashes structured tree plus boundary.
limitations: Source explicitly says Lean tree proofs do not verify this Rust implementation or serialization.
Foundation PlanarTree hashes use a different weaker scheme; demonstrated collision does not establish kernel-normalized hash collision.

claims.claim: Runtime inventory interpretation locally executes only identity, pair and checked i64 sum; selected host guards or unregistered external targets refuse local execution.
dependencies: trusted external executor for other bindings
limitations: VALID can describe an inert normalized plan with no execution.
No native mechanism here executes arbitrary skill prose or verifies a QM derivation.
Runtime limits and downstream type semantics still need broader adversarial audit.

claims.claim: Generic L4 capacity records and trivial Ok/Err assertions are not module-wide correctness or mutation-analysis evidence.
dependencies: separate reproducible mutation campaign if claimed
limitations: Comments saying killed=6 do not execute six mutations.
Capacity-record tests exercise their own tiny admission wrapper, not surrounding algorithm behavior.

claims.claim: OperadAlgebra recursively evaluates supplied JSON actions or structural packaging; its carrier strings and policy reference do not validate runtime value types or enforce an admission decision.
limitations: Evaluation receipts bind term ID only, reuse a fixed timestamp, and do not bind distinct input/execution occurrence identities.
No general algebra homomorphism, authority or execution-provenance theorem established.

findings.title: Reversed attestation interval panics before signature verification
findings.observation: issued_at100, expires_at50, otherwise valid policy/binding, empty signature: verify panics in debug build rather than returning Refusal.
findings.mechanism: valid_lifetime eagerly subtracts unsigned timestamps even when valid_issue is false.
findings.limits: No signed-attestation acceptance bypass shown. Release overflow behavior was not tested; with unchecked wrapping valid_issue still fails.
findings.repair: Use checked duration or short-circuit on invalid interval before subtraction; regression must cover malformed unsigned endpoints.

findings.title: Foundation tree hashes conflate structurally different trees
findings.observation: Nullary operation id f;leaf:A and unary operation id f with A input both hash to tree_14fe719ba34ee24b; arities0 and1.
findings.mechanism: Unescaped semicolon concatenation is noninjective before hashing; output signature and many operation fields are omitted, and hash is truncated to64bits.
findings.limits: Distinct from kernel::terms canonical structured hash. No collision in that stronger path demonstrated.
findings.repair: Use domain-separated structured encoding with complete identity assumptions and full digest; migrate existing IDs explicitly.

findings.title: Permutation operation IDs collide for different valid permutations
findings.observation: For12 inputs, [1,11,0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10] and [11,1,0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10] produce p^sigma_11102345678910 despite different signatures.
findings.mechanism: Decimal indices are concatenated without separators.
findings.limits: ID collision, not cryptographic hash collision or demonstrated authority bypass.
findings.repair: Encode permutation as a framed vector or canonical structured digest.

findings.title: Duplicate parent edges break stochastic rank reconstruction
findings.observation: P,C with repeated P->C gives transition row sums1 and3/4. Dense solver returns [1/2,1/2], rejected by its own certificate verifier. Compatibility matrix port returns the same defective row.
findings.mechanism: Denominator counts duplicate parents while membership adds each destination's contribution once.
findings.limits: Verifier rejects this dense output; no false verification of this example. Sparse citation solver handles multiplicities separately.
findings.repair: Reject/deduplicate edges consistently or accumulate multiplicity in numerators; validate rows and solver certificate.

findings.title: Singleton sparse PageRank skips graph validation
findings.observation: CitationGraph::new(1,[(0,99)]) returns accepted/converged rank with zero error instead of rejecting out-of-range endpoint.
findings.limits: Rank of the valid singleton graph is trivially1; the defect is certifying an invalid declared graph.
findings.repair: Validate graph endpoints before singleton shortcut.

findings.title: Thymus panel digest does not bind sample boundaries
findings.observation: Panels [a newline b] and [a,b] have identical self_panel_hash despite different sample counts1 and2.
findings.mechanism: A newline delimiter is also permitted inside samples.
findings.limits: samples_tested differs, so complete verdicts need not collide. No authenticated panel-custody bypass demonstrated.
findings.repair: Hash a framed ordered sequence of samples rather than delimiter concatenation.

findings.title: Adding an ancestor leaves descendant generations stale
findings.observation: Insert valid-seal B->C, then A->B: B generation1, C generation1 although max-parent-plus-one requires2. BFS distance remains correct.
findings.mechanism: Only direct child cache is updated; derive_generation returns positive cached value without checking new ancestor structure.
findings.limits: Fixture uses legal incremental insertions; no concurrent or persisted graph behavior tested.
findings.repair: Invalidate/rederive descendant generations or enforce an insertion invariant that prevents stale caches.

findings.title: EIS activation-use-case parity target does not compile
findings.observation: Rust1.99.0 reports E0621 for input lifetime and E0597 for trace borrow at final expression. Whole selected --tests invocation yields no test results.
findings.repair: Repair test lifetime/borrow structure and then run all intended vectors; source implementation was not edited.

findings.title: Current native suites contain obsolete digests and witness fixtures
findings.observation: Two immunity tests use w1/w2/w rejected by bound witness admission; genome test expects omega-prefixed digest; two canonical tests pass core.test but expect omega.test; two EIS activation tests retain old receipt hashes. Current Python canonical_id matches native first danger-row hash dca5bb..., not frozen84c5cc....
findings.limits: Only the first mismatching EIS row was independently recomputed. No complete fixture migration or historical custody reconstruction.
findings.repair: Preserve old fixture provenance, regenerate current namespace vectors from an explicit versioned rule and repair stale witness construction; rerun whole relevant suites.
